review_cost.rationale: Approve with nits: a couple of structural suggestions (move formatting helpers out of api.ts, memoise getDex) and small fixes (focus preservation, aria-live scope) that don't block the merge.

findings.issue: getDex() re-derives the full 1,025-entry dex (species index, ~2k type slots, generation map, sort) on every home request; only the underlying HTTP fetches are cached.
findings.suggestion: Memoise the derived DexEntry[] alongside the cache with the same FRESH_MS policy, so each request is a filter over a reused array.

findings.issue: Two data-loading styles coexist: /pokemon/:name loads via loadPokemon in the route handler (where 404 is decided), while Move/Ability/Type pages receive their primary resource from the handler but load supplementary data inside async components (details.tsx:22, 116).
findings.suggestion: Pick one convention — either load everything in handlers and pass plain props to (synchronous) components, or commit to async-component loading everywhere — so 404 decisions and error handling live in one place.

findings.issue: hx-swap="outerHTML" on #moves-body replaces the game <select> itself, so keyboard focus is lost after changing the game.
findings.suggestion: Mark the select with hx-preserve, or split the form out of the swapped fragment and target only the tables.

findings.issue: aria-live="polite" wraps the entire results region, so every debounced filter change re-announces up to 48 card names to screen-reader users.
findings.suggestion: Scope the live region to a small status node (e.g. the 'N Pokémon' count) and leave the card list outside it.

findings.issue: withSlot decrements active and wakes a queued waiter, but a concurrently arriving request can take the freed slot first, so MAX_CONCURRENT can be exceeded (harmless, but the invariant is silently soft).
findings.suggestion: Hand the slot directly to the waiter (increment active before resolving) or note the overshoot in a comment.

findings.issue: Presentation helpers (humanize, dexNumber, spriteUrl, cleanText) live in the HTTP/data layer, so components import formatting from the API module.
findings.suggestion: Move name/number formatting into components.tsx (or a small format.ts) and keep api.ts about fetching and API shapes.

findings.issue: Static assets are served with Cache-Control max-age=3600 but have no versioned filenames or ETag, so post-deploy visitors can get stale CSS/JS for up to an hour.
findings.suggestion: Fingerprint filenames at build time (copy-assets.mjs is the natural place) or use a content-hash query string.

findings.issue: mapAll is an alias for Promise.all(items.map(fn)); the comment claims a concurrency limit that actually comes from get()'s semaphore, so the indirection misleads readers.
findings.suggestion: Delete mapAll and call Promise.all directly, or make it genuinely enforce the limit.

findings.issue: homeUrl accepts page both on the query object and as a second parameter (index.tsx:44 passes both), which is easy to misuse.
findings.suggestion: Take only the override parameter, or only the query object.

findings.issue: The fallback pattern typeLabels.get(x) ?? humanize(x) is repeated in five places (details.tsx:34,132; pokemon.tsx:69,260; home.tsx:72).
findings.suggestion: Add a single labelFor(typeLabels, name) helper next to TypeBadge.

summary: A genuinely idiomatic current-stable Hono + htmx app: async JSX server components, server-chosen partials with HX-Push-Url, history-restore handling, hx-sync race suppression, noscript fallbacks, and a carefully engineered stale-while-revalidate cache with bounded size and concurrency. Remaining work is nits — one data-loading convention instead of two, a memoised getDex, focus/live-region polish and asset cache-busting — none of which would hold up a merge.
